newsitem.title: GERMANY: Firm dollar lifts German shares to record highs.
newsitem.headline: Firm dollar lifts German shares to record highs.

text.p: German shares hit record highs on Wednesday as blue chip shares got a strong boost from the firm dollar, always a plus for a market thronged by export-driven firms.
The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade up 34.91 points at a record close of 3,854.76 points after reaching a new all-time high at 3,871.13 points early in the session.
The market notched up more gains in after-bourse trade, which the IBIS DAX closed at 3,867.53 points, up 32.69 points.
"The pretty strong dollar has really given this market a fresh outlook," said one Frankfurt trader of a dollar which breached the key psychological level of 1.75 marks in European dealings.
Chemical and financial shares were among the heaviest traded.
Hoechst ended bourse trade up one mark at 79.30 marks while BASF AG ended bourse down one pfennig at 66.05 marks. Bayer AG was up 45 pfennigs at 70.75 marks.
Hoechst had risen nearly six percent on Tuesday on fresh buy recommendations from some brokerage houses.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said on Wednesday it had lowered some earnings estimates for Bayer and BASF AG and had reduced its earnings estimates for Hoechst for 1997 but had raised its estimates for Hoechst for 1998 and 1999.
The recommendation on all three of the major German chemical groups remained unchanged at "neutral" but with a higher weighting for Hoechst within the sector, DMG said.
Deutsche Bank AG helped lead the advance and reached a new all-time high at 105.35 marks in bourse dealings. Deutsche shares ended bourse trade up 2.75 marks at 104.80 marks.
Rivals Commerzbank AG and Dresdner Bank AG were also higher, with Commerzbank up one mark at 50.15 marks and Dresdner up 1.35 pfennigs at 62.60 marks.
